packageDirectories.versionDescription: Native terminal error logging. Every job now emits exactly one job-level entry describing how it ended - ERROR for 'Failed' and 'Completed with Errors', INFO for 'Completed' and 'Cancelled' - across all terminal paths (worker completion, zero records, CSV middleware failure, coordinator retry exhaustion, kill switch), with no worker code. CursorBatchCompletionHandler previously built its logger with CursorBatchLogger.getDefault(), hardcoded to System.debug, so the one class that decides terminal job status never reached the org's logging adapter; it now resolves the adapter and tags entries from CursorBatch_Config__mdt.Logger_Tag__c, falling back to 'CursorBatch Completion' when blank. Every framework error also carries a scope, both as a message prefix and as a tag next to Logger_Tag__c: JOB FAILED, JOB COMPLETED WITH ERRORS, JOB FINISH FAILED, JOB CHAIN FAILED, WORKER FAILED. That matters most for JOB FINISH FAILED, because metadata-driven jobs reflect the once-per-job finish() callback onto the worker class, so those failures previously read like one of the N per-page worker failures. A finish() failure now logs once with its stack trace instead of two or three times. Uncatchable platform aborts are enriched from AsyncApexJob.ExtendedStatus via FinalizerContext.getAsyncApexJobId() in both finalizers, so 'System.UnexpectedException: connection was cancelled here' now carries the underlying '[QUERY_TIMEOUT] Your query request was running for too long.'; the code is parsed generically into a 'CursorBatch Failure QUERY_TIMEOUT' tag and flows through to the job record and the terminal entry. Recovery is best-effort, falling back to the exception alone when ExtendedStatus is not yet committed. Worker failures reaching the completion handler are summarized as one entry per job per platform-event batch rather than one per event, so log volume and DML no longer scale with the subscriber batch size. CursorBatchCoordinator now resolves the adapter in both constructors and memoizes config per transaction. Finally, the finish() path now tags the logger a subclass uses. Both invokeFinishCallback methods construct the worker or coordinator by reflection purely to call finish(), so initialize() never runs on a worker and the tagging constructor never runs on a coordinator; anything a subclass logged inside finish() was therefore untagged, and subscribers were re-calling setLogger() inside finish() to work around it. initializeFinishState() and initializeJobName() now apply Logger_Tag__c additively via Callable, so those workarounds can be removed without losing tags. BREAKING GUIDANCE CHANGE: those workarounds must be removed, not merely can be. A setLogger() call inside finish() now runs after the framework has tagged the logger and replaces the tagged instance with an untagged one, stripping Logger_Tag__c from everything logged afterwards. setLogger() is no longer needed anywhere: a worker or coordinator with no constructor at all resolves CursorBatchLoggerAdapter by convention and is tagged on both the processing path and the finish path, with Logger_Tag__c on the job's CursorBatch_Config__mdt record as the single place a tag is configured. Docs updated accordingly, and unpackaged/classes/NebulaLoggerAdapterForCursorBatch.cls is removed - it was reachable only through an explicit setLogger() call, was not named for convention-based discovery, and did not implement Callable, so it could never receive Logger_Tag__c. Use unpackaged/classes/CursorBatchLoggerAdapter.cls instead.
